# RELEASE

Frees a machine, operator or other resource that an earlier SEIZE gave the entity, after an optional delay.

Release everything the entity holds under `resource_name` (a plain resource or a set member), after an optional delay. Pairs with SEIZE for a hold split across two blocks; raises if the entity never seized that name (fail-loud by design).

Family: resource. Python builder: `m.release(...)`.

## Typical uses

Use RELEASE to free a resource that an earlier [SEIZE](seize.md) or a PROCESS with the action `Seize Delay` gave the entity. It ends a hold that spans several blocks. A PROCESS with the default action frees its own resource, so it needs no RELEASE.

## Behaviour and rules

The block waits for its optional delay and then frees every unit the entity holds under `resource_name`. For a set, it frees the member that was chosen at the seize. Naming a fleet frees a vehicle that a TRANSPORT kept.

If the entity holds nothing under that name, the run stops with an error that names the entity and the resource. This is deliberate, so a missing SEIZE does not pass unnoticed. A resource name that is not declared is also caught by a check.

The end of a SEIZE and RELEASE pair blocks like the end of a PROCESS. If the next block has a finite space, a finished part keeps its resource until the space accepts it. A worker that leaves when the work ends is the one exception, unless `worker_when_blocked` is `stays`.

The hold is recorded when it ends, so the busy time, the busy cost and the schedule log all count from the seize to this block.

## Ports

- Inputs: any number of incoming links.
- Outputs: one outgoing link.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `resource_name` | str | `''` | yes |  |  | Name of the resource or resource set to release. |
| `worker_when_blocked` | str | `'leaves'` |  |  |  | What the worker does while this station holds a finished part that nothing downstream has room for. "leaves" (the default): the worker is free when the work ends. "stays": the worker waits with the part and is free when it is accepted downstream. The same either way where nothing downstream is finite. |

## Problem codes

A check of the model reports these about this block:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_RESOURCE_UNKNOWN` | A SEIZE/PROCESS/RELEASE block's resource_name names no declared resource or resource set. |
| `W_TRANSPORT_KEEP_UNFREED` | Nothing downstream of a TRANSPORT with keep_vehicle frees the vehicle (no RELEASE naming the fleet, no TRANSPORT on it without keep_vehicle): it waits with the part until the part leaves. |

## Example

The snippet seeds itself; its output is from a run made when this page was generated.

```python
from nagasim import build as nb

m = nb.Model(time_limit=480, warmup=60)
m.add_resource(name="Dock")
arrive = m.create(distribution=nb.Exponential(rate=0.2))
arrive >> m.seize(resource_name="Dock") >> m.delay(distribution=nb.Constant(value=3)) >> m.release(resource_name="Dock") >> m.dispose()

results = m.run(seed=1)
print(int(results.kpi("resource/Dock/Total Seizes")), "seizes; each ended by the RELEASE block")
```

```text
79 seizes; each ended by the RELEASE block
```
